 EPFO Approves SWP for PF Retirees, Cuts Minimum Balance Requirement to 10%
 -->
 Updated on November 20, 2026 Posted by Subodh Kumawat Posted in Taxes in India 3 Minutes Read 
 The Employees Provident Fund Organisation has finally given the nod to a Systematic Withdrawal Plan during its 240th Central Board of Trustees meeting held on November 19, 2026, which means retiring folks no longer have to take their entire PF money out in one giant lump sum.
 For years, people hitting retirement age had to file for a final settlement and suddenly had lakhs or even crores sitting in their bank account, which sounded great at first but created plenty of real headaches. 
 Read Also: Easy Guide to Online PF Transfer Via EPFO Portal with FAQs 
 A lot of retirees ended up stressed about where to safely invest such a big amount without getting trapped in shady schemes or losing ground to inflation, while others simply spent too much too early and felt the pinch later on when medical bills started piling up.
 With this new voluntary SWP option, subscribers can draw their savings in regular instalments like monthly, quarterly, or half-yearly payouts while keeping the rest of their balance parked inside the EPF account.
 The biggest advantage here is that whatever money stays in the account keeps earning that reliable, government-backed EPF interest instead of stopping the moment you retire. It basically works like a steady, self-made pension flow without forcing people to pull everything out before they actually need it.
 According to the Labour Ministry, around 6.32 lakh members above 55 years of age who hold more than ₹5 lakh in PF savings are expected to benefit first, and if a subscriber passes away during the payout period, their nominee or dependent can either withdraw the remaining balance or continue receiving the instalments.
 Alongside the SWP rollout, the board also eased existing withdrawal rules by slashing the minimum balance requirement from 25 per cent down to 10 per cent for members up to 55 years of age. Earlier, subscribers under 55 had to keep at least 25 per cent of their eligible PF contributions earmarked in the account at all times, which capped partial withdrawals at 75 per cent.
 Cutting that buffer to 10 per cent means working members can now potentially access up to 90 per cent of their eligible balance for approved needs while still leaving a small cushion earning interest, whereas once you retire after turning 55, the option to withdraw 100 per cent of your corpus remains completely intact. 
 Recommended : Easy Way to Check PF Balance & Download Passbook via WhatsApp 
 To add further relief for workers facing a sudden financial crunch, the waiting period for final provident fund settlement after losing a job has also been reduced from 12 months to just 2 months, though the waiting window for final pension withdrawal stays unchanged at 36 months.
 Since fewer private sector jobs come with old-school pensions and people are living longer than they used to, a lot of working professionals depend heavily on their provident fund as their main safety net in old age.
 Letting retirees pace their withdrawals while giving active subscribers easier access to their own money offers way better control over household expenses and helps savings last longer. All these approvals will come into effect once the official scheme amendments and operational guidelines are formally notified on the member portal.
